brief: 6 quiet decisions that kill startups — and the founders that survived each one.

slots.body: Silent choices sink companies before they ever see the iceberg. Learn the patterns from founders who barely made it out.
You polish for months while the market moves on. Founders who survive kill the ego and ship ugly truth to users fast.
slots.quote: If you aren't embarrassed, you shipped too late.

slots.body: Revenue climbs but margins bleed out in the dark. Survivors pull the plug on vanity metrics before the cash runs dry.
slots.quote: Growth without profit is just a slow death.

slots.body: A bloated team kills speed and burns runway overnight. Smart founders hire slow, fire fast, and protect the culture.
slots.quote: Every wrong hire steals oxygen from the right ones.

slots.body: One-off promises bloat your roadmap into an unreadable mess. The best teams build for the few, not the loudest voice.
slots.quote: Focus is saying no to a thousand good ideas.

slots.body: You become the bottleneck and the single point of failure. Survivors build systems so the company outlives their mood.
slots.quote: Delegate the outcome, not just the task.

slots.body: Attachment to the original idea clouds every dashboard red flag. Founders who live know when to burn the plan and run.
slots.quote: Pivoting late is just failing with extra steps.

slots.body: Share this with a founder who needs to hear it before it's too late.
